text.p: Following are the main stories in Slovenia's Monday morning newspapers:
- Number of Bosnian refugees in Slovenia will fall to 5,300 after July 31 when the government is expected to cease the refugee status for 2,000 refugees.

- Some 91 percent of Slovenia's coastal tourist facilities were occupied over the weekend. The number of foreign guests increased by 17 percent, while the number of domestic visitors fell by 19 percent compared to the same weekend in 1996.
- Consumer prices in Slovenia increased by almost nine percent since March, a research published by Delo showed.
- Insurance company Triglav is the largest in Slovenia with a 50 percent share of the market. Insurance Maribor comes in second with 20 percent, followed by Adriatic with 10 percent.
- The Christian Democrats, which hold nine out of 90 parliamentary seats, on Sunday reelected Lojze Peterle for the post of the new president of the party.
- Minister of Agriculture Ciril Smrkolj met his Hungarian counterpart Frigyes Nagy to discuss positions of the two countries within the Central European Free Trade Association (CEFTA).
